claims.text: Varying the relative concentrations of magnetic and nonmagnetic elements in non-equiatomic HEAs tunes the balance of magnetic exchange interactions.
Tuning exchange interactions through composition can optimize the magnetic ordering temperature.
Tuning exchange interactions through composition can optimize the magnetocaloric effect.
The initial material is a non-equiatomic high-entropy alloy containing both magnetic and nonmagnetic elements.
Systematically varying the concentration of key magnetic elements during synthesis is the proposed tuning method.
Compositional changes alter the alloy microstructure.
Compositional changes alter local atomic environments in the alloy.
Changing elemental ratios adjusts electron density.
Changing elemental ratios adjusts magnetic exchange interactions.
Changes in electron density and exchange interactions affect the magnetic ordering temperature.
Changes in electron density and exchange interactions affect the magnitude of the magnetocaloric effect by modifying entropy change near magnetic transitions.
Compositionally tuned samples are predicted to exhibit a shift in magnetic transition temperature relative to the baseline composition.
Compositionally tuned samples are predicted to exhibit enhanced isothermal magnetic entropy change relative to the baseline composition.
Extreme processing or environmental conditions may cause deviations from the predicted behavior.
